title: System Information Discovery
summary: System Information Discovery is the collection of host-level detail such as operating system name and version, build, patch and hotfix level, hardware architecture, hostname, and domain membership. An adversary uses that detail to decide whether a foothold is worth keeping and which later technique will work against it, so the behaviour typically appears very early and often as one burst of commands from a single process. On network devices the same result comes from the vendor command interface, and in infrastructure-as-a-service clouds it comes from authenticated provider API calls that describe the instance or its image. The artefact is mundane, which is the difficulty, because inventory agents and administrators run comparable commands. Discrimination comes from context: the parent process, the user, the host's role, and whether the same host was also probed for users, networks, and files within seconds.

beginner.definition: This is the act of learning what a computer is. The attacker checks the operating system, its version, the updates it has, and the type of hardware. It is like reading the label on a machine before deciding how to use it. This is a discovery technique, which means it gathers information rather than causing damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing the exact version tells an attacker which weaknesses may exist. Knowing the patch level tells them whether an old flaw is still open. This step usually comes before the real attack, so catching it early can stop everything else. The commands look harmless on their own, which makes them easy to miss. You need context, not just the command itself.
howItWorks: The attacker runs built-in tools on the host to read the operating system name and version.
They check the installed updates and hotfixes to find any missing security patches.
They collect hardware details, such as the processor type, memory size and system architecture.
On servers and appliances they use vendor command interfaces to read firmware and model data.
In cloud environments they call provider interfaces that describe the virtual machine and its image.
Defenders look for these commands running together, outside maintenance windows, under unusual accounts.
beginner.example: Picture a burglar who first walks past a house and notes the locks, the alarm box and the age of the windows. Nothing is broken and nothing is taken. They are simply deciding which house is worth the effort and which tools to bring. System information discovery is that walk past the house, and it usually comes just before the break-in attempt.
takeaways: Version and patch data help an attacker choose a target, so keep systems current.
Harmless commands become suspicious when many of them run together on one host.
Combine command logs with user and host context before you decide.

objectives: Describe the kinds of system detail an adversary collects on a host.
Explain how that detail shapes the later stages of an intrusion.
Identify log sources that record discovery commands, such as process creation events.
Distinguish routine administrative checks from hostile discovery activity.
Explain how patching and asset management reduce the value of this information.
